# WikiKit Documentation

A robots.txt-style index of the WikiKit documentation for LLMs. WikiKit is a
headless, AI-native knowledge system for humans and agents: Markdown-first
knowledge in, structured and agent-ready knowledge out. Sources are archived
verbatim, an LLM synthesizes maintained concept pages with verifiable claims
and citations, every change passes a human review gate as a ChangeProposal,
and the knowledge is reachable over HTTP/REST and MCP and exportable as
Markdown or OKF bundles. Each entry below has a title, path, and one-line
summary. For the complete documentation inlined into a single file, see
[docs/llms-full.txt](docs/llms-full.txt).

> Default local base URL: http://127.0.0.1:4060 — OpenAPI 3.1 spec at
> `/openapi.json`, MCP (Streamable HTTP) at `POST /mcp`. Authenticate with
> `Authorization: Bearer wk_...` or `X-API-Key: wk_...`; scopes are
> `knowledge:read`, `knowledge:propose`, `knowledge:review`, `knowledge:approve`, `admin` (approve implies review).

## Start here

- [Built-in agent guide](docs/agent-guide.md): WikiKit's code-versioned system knowledge — operating model, dynamic space routing, and capability-based no-CLI setup for MCP clients (live at `/agent-guide.md`).
- [README](README.md): What WikiKit is (the LLM-wiki loop, curation over collection), zero-config quickstart, standards-only integration, and links to everything else.
- [Coding-agent integration](docs/coding-agent-integration.md): Product-neutral lifecycle contract — compact startup grounding, task-dynamic additional spaces, and review-gated session learnings; example hooks for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor plus a served agent hooks installer (`GET /install.sh`, `GET /install.ps1`).
- [Example sources](examples/README.md): Two example source documents to ingest and the concept frontmatter reference for export/import bundles.
- [Concept frontmatter reference](examples/concept-frontmatter-reference.md): The lossless claims/relations frontmatter format used by `?format=md` bundles.

## API & usage

- Endpoints: `GET /v1/spaces`, `POST /v1/spaces`, `GET /v1/agent/briefing`, `POST /v1/agent/context`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/settings`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/charter`, `PUT /v1/spaces/{space}/charter`, `DELETE /v1/spaces/{space}/charter`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/charter/versions`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/ingest`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/ingest/document`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/agent/sessions`, `GET /v1/ingests/{id}`, `GET /v1/ingests/{id}/triage`, `POST /v1/ingests/{id}/triage`, `POST /v1/ingests/{id}/triage/resolve`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/ingests`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/sources`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/sources/{id}`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/source-streams`, `DELETE /v1/spaces/{space}/source-streams/{external_source_id}`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/decisions`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/decisions/{slug}`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/history`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/neighbors`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/deleted-concepts`, `DELETE /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/restore`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/search`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/query`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/outputs`, `GET /v1/outputs/{id}`, `POST /v1/outputs/{id}/promote`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/health`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/attention`, `PUT /v1/spaces/{space}/attention/{key}`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/schedules`, `PUT /v1/spaces/{space}/schedules`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/proposals`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/proposals`, `GET /v1/proposals/{id}`, `POST /v1/proposals/{id}/approve`, `POST /v1/proposals/{id}/reject`, `POST /v1/proposals/{id}/split`, `POST /v1/proposals/{id}/request-changes`, `GET /v1/proposals/{id}/lint`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/lint`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/export`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/import`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks`, `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`, `GET /v1/stats/overview`, `GET /v1/stats/mcp`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/http`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/usage`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/coverage`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/reviews`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/ingests`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/knowledge`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/llm`, `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/stats/webhooks`, `GET /v1/api-keys`, `POST /v1/api-keys`, `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`, `GET /v1/identities`, `PUT /v1/identities/{provider}/{subject}`, `DELETE /v1/identities/{provider}/{subject}`, `GET /v1/installation/knowledge-config`, `GET /health`, `GET /ready`, `GET /metrics`, `GET /.well-known/service-descriptor.json`, `GET /openapi.json`, `GET /review/{id}`, `GET /agent-guide.md`, `GET /llms.txt`, `GET /llms-full.txt`, `GET /.well-known/llms.txt`, `GET /.well-known/llms-full.txt`, `GET /install.sh`, `GET /install.ps1`, `GET /install/hooks/{script}`.
- Ingest is asynchronous: `202` + a `Location` header to poll; the result is a pending ChangeProposal. Approval is a separate, deliberate call.
- Items of `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/concepts` carry `evidence: {claims, uncited_claims, sources}` over visible claims only (`verified|disputed|deprecated` — staged claims are not knowledge), so an agent can tell which page is backed by sources before fetching it; `claims: 0` is a page written by hand without any. The object is ABSENT — never zeroed — on a reference-target page, a row an import created to receive relations, which has no knowledge to measure; absence means "not measured" and must never be read as a zero. Such a row carries `not_measured: {reason}` in its place, so the reason travels with the row instead of being inferred from the hole: `reason: "reference_target"` today, plus `withheld_claims` when that page nevertheless holds visible claims — the count the measurement would have reported, and never `sources` or `uncited_claims`, because "how well is this page backed" is not a question a reference target has an answer to. A row carrying NEITHER field is a page that stopped being readable; treat an unrecognised `reason` as a refusal you cannot explain rather than as a reference target. Which revision markers make a page a reference target is per-installation configuration (`WIKIKIT_SCAFFOLDING_KINDS`, plus WikiKit's built-in `structural-reference`), so the meaning of an absence is portable while the set of pages that produce one is not; `GET /v1/installation/knowledge-config` (admin) reports the markers one installation actually honours, each attributed `built_in` (WikiKit's own) or `configured` (the installation declared it). `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/search` carries the same object on `kind: "concept"` hits — same counts, same visible claims — so the choice of which page to open is as informed from a search as from the index; `claim` hits and `source_chunk` hits carry no `evidence` (a source-evidence hit is unreviewed archive material, not approved knowledge).
- OpenAPI 3.1 is generated live from the route registry — fetch the spec at `/openapi.json`; a committed snapshot lives in [docs/openapi.json](docs/openapi.json).
- MCP (Streamable HTTP, outside the REST surface): tools `wikikit_guide`, `wikikit_spaces`, `wikikit_briefing`, `wikikit_context`, `wikikit_search`, `wikikit_read`, `wikikit_sources`, `wikikit_decisions`, `wikikit_history`, `wikikit_lint`, `wikikit_health`, `wikikit_overview`, `wikikit_outputs`, `wikikit_ingest`, `wikikit_ingest_status`, `wikikit_propose`, `wikikit_promote_output`, `wikikit_proposals`, `wikikit_review_proposal` — scope-gated visibility; `wikikit_health` is one LLM-free read of lint findings, coverage, the review queue with the age of its oldest change and the live ingest queue; `wikikit_outputs` reads what the wiki produced (answers, scheduled briefings, health reports) and `wikikit_promote_output` files one back in as a source — through the ordinary pipeline, so a human still approves the change; `wikikit_context` is the zero-config task entry point when no hook supplied context; review requires `knowledge:review` (implied by `knowledge:approve`; the REST approve/reject endpoints still demand `knowledge:approve`), inspection of the full diff — including relations added and, via a proposal's `relations_removed`, staged removals of active relations — and a human-owned decision collected through native MCP elicitation. The review tool accepts only `proposal_id`; passing `decision`/`note` as arguments is refused with `approval_requires_human`. On a client with `elicitation.form` (the primary channel — in a terminal client the in-terminal review dialog) the human owns approve/reject plus the optional note in the native form. Only when the form is unavailable or provably unrendered does the tool fall back to `elicitation.url`: it sends the human to the review page (`GET /review/{id}?via=elicitation`) and returns `outcome: "url_review_started"` immediately; the decision lands out of band with the reviewer's own key, is audited as `review_channel: "url_elicitation"`, and the server signals `notifications/elicitation/complete` (polling `wikikit_proposals` stays the fallback). On a client without elicitation the tool returns `outcome: "human_review_required"` with a `review_url` — the human opens that page, authenticates with their own reviewer key and decides there; the agent polls `wikikit_proposals`; with a review-scoped key it never approves through chat or REST for the human, while a key deliberately granted `knowledge:approve` sanctions executing the user's explicit chat instruction over REST. Decline, cancel, timeout or invalid data likewise leaves the proposal pending.
- MCP self-description: `initialize` returns usage `instructions`; the tools-only-compatible `wikikit_guide` and resource `wikikit://system/agent-guide` expose immutable product guidance; `resources/list` + `resources/read` also serve this file (`wikikit://docs/llms.txt`) and the full docs (`wikikit://docs/llms-full.txt`) — no HTTP GET required.
- Remote MCP OAuth: `/mcp` exposes protected-resource discovery, dynamic client registration and PKCE. The `mcp-auth-v2` chooser always shows `Continue with SSO` first and `Continue with API key` second. `GET /v1/identity/providers`, `POST /v1/identity/sessions`, and the generic start/callback/logout routes form the provider-neutral public boundary; there are no provider-named or legacy aliases. API key and direct OIDC are configured and operated independently by WikiKit. Session exchange is `{provider_id,identity_token}` → `{api_key,principal_id,context_id,email}`; email is nullable and only provider-verified email is retained. OIDC requires `sub` plus an exact configured subject or verified-email allow-list match. Operator sessions are bounded and revocable; interactive grants are request-bounded by `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_ALLOWED_SCOPES` and per-provider policy.
- Cockpit (the one human interface): a React console the same binary serves at `/cockpit`, built into the artifact (`assets/cockpit` → `src/cockpit-embedded.ts`, drift-checked). It presents a space as a wiki, a concept as a Markdown page, and an edit as a change proposal — the submit button says "Submit change", because nothing a human writes becomes knowledge without a `knowledge:approve` decision. It reaches only the documented `/v1` routes and holds no credential: `GET /v1/session` answers `{"session": null}` for an anonymous tab and never 401s, `GET /v1/identity/cockpit-login?return_to=<path under /cockpit>` enters the same provider chooser every other sign-in uses (the console is deliberately not an OAuth client — no consent screen for one's own console), and `DELETE /v1/session` signs out. The resulting HttpOnly operator cookie is a FALLBACK credential on `/v1`, consulted only when no `Authorization`/`X-API-Key` header is present, with a same-origin `Origin` required on unsafe methods. Agents are unaffected: no route changes shape, and there is no console API.
- Interactive review clients: the native form is the primary channel — Codex should set `approval_policy = { granular = { mcp_elicitations = true } }` and `approvals_reviewer = "user"`; Claude Code requires 2.1.76+; ChatGPT support is conditional on the active connector advertising native form elicitation and passing a post-deploy canary. A client advertising `elicitation.url` (MCP 2025-11-25) gains the URL-mode fallback — a yes/no consent, the browser review page, and a completion notification — used only when the form is unavailable or auto-cancelled without rendering. Without any elicitation capability the review hands off (`human_review_required` with a `review_url`): the human opens the review page and decides there as themselves, and the agent sees the result via `wikikit_proposals`.
- Usage analytics: opt in with `WIKIKIT_USAGE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` plus `WIKIKIT_USAGE_HMAC_SECRET`. The ledger captures controlled HTTP/MCP/knowledge/review dimensions and exact product-local HMAC adoption only—never content, prompts, queries, tool arguments/results, raw URLs, IP/UA, credentials or dynamic ids. Raw retention is `WIKIKIT_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`; aggregate readers support bounded UTC windows, traffic class and max-two groupings.

## Operating & deployment

- [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md): Every environment variable with its default — 12-factor, `WIKIKIT_*` prefix, production guards, zero-config dev defaults.
- [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md): Single self-contained Bun binary, self-migrating boot, systemd, `/health` + `/ready` probes, graceful drain, release pipeline.
- [Security](SECURITY.md): Reporting vulnerabilities; operator hardening notes (key pepper, scoped keys, webhook signature verification, SSRF guard).
- [.env.example](.env.example): Annotated template of every configuration variable settable via `.env` (`NODE_ENV` is process-env only).

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): Request lifecycle, the `src/` module map, the proposal mechanics (staged rows + atomic SQL flip), ingest pipeline, MCP session model, and drift detection.

- [OKF v0.1 spec](docs/okf-v0.1.md): The vendored Open Knowledge Format specification the OKF export/import conforms to.
